key_insight: A backward-mapping, genome-guided workflow can translate device-level targets into interpretable chemical design rules for discovering phase-stable, lead-free double perovskites.
engineering_relevance: The framework narrows a 13,088-composition search space to seven DFT-validated candidates, offering a practical inverse-design route for safer halide perovskite optoelectronic materials.
method: Started with 13,088 charge-balanced A2BB'X6 compositions and applied halide-aware geometric formability filtering.
Encoded six families of chemical-genome descriptors and trained evolutionary-optimized ML surrogates for stability and band gap prediction.
Used SHAP interpretation and DFT phenotype closure to validate candidates and extract design rules.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports DFT validation of seven finalists, including stability, band-edge character, effective masses, dielectric response, optical absorption, conductivity, reflectivity, energy-loss spectra, and XRD fingerprints.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on scalar-relativistic PBE band gaps and surrogate-model screening, so transferability to experiments and higher-level electronic-structure methods should be checked.
paper_title: Backward Mapping from Device Targets to Chemical Genomes for Interpretable Discovery of Phase-Stable Lead-Free Double Perovskites with DFT-Validated Design Rules
